questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always wanted to visit Edinburgh. The culture and the landscape of Scotland were my main reasons, as well as the fact that the language wouldn't be a problem.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: At arrival, easy enough - before going, very difficult!!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not a lot, but I didn't need it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not a lot of help, I was told wrong things when contacting the University.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: International check in with pre-booked time slots at campus. Very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, but that was only because of help from the contact person in Copenhagen - she basically did it for me after I hadn't received ANY information from the host information a month before arrival.

questions.answer: Much more discussion and participation-based teaching.

questions.answer:
US grand strategy and foreign policy
Politics of Post-Soviet Russia
Survey in Middle Eastern Politics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
US grand strategy and foreign policy
Politics of Post-Soviet Russia

It's not that Survey in Middle Eastern Politics was a bad course at all, but the 20-person discussion every week wasn't to my liking.

questions.answer: Pretty difficult, but just talk to them and be persistent.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for a very high rent. 
Uni work takes a lot more time than in Copenhagen.
Just talk to people, they're very friendly.
